prompt: Implement scalar_ir(program, choices), a deterministic tagged-value analyzer for a small LLVM 18.1.8-inspired scalar subset. It is not an LLVM text parser, verifier, optimizer or machine execution. program is a native list of at most 32 exact-schema records. Every value-defining record has a fresh case-sensitive ASCII id matching [A-Za-z0-9_]{1,12}; operands name earlier definitions. Optional {op:'br',condition:ID} has no result ID and may occur only once, as the last record. Other records: {op:'literal',id,bits,kind,value}, where bits is an int 1–8, kind is 'value', 'poison' or 'undef', and value is an unsigned bit pattern 0<=value<2**bits for kind='value', otherwise None; {op:'add',id,lhs:ID,rhs:ID,nsw:bool}; {op:'eq',id,lhs:ID,rhs:ID}; {op:'select',id,cond:ID,yes:ID,no:ID}; {op:'freeze',id,value:ID}. Integer domains exclude bool. add/eq operands have equal bit widths; select cond and br condition have width 1, and select arms have equal widths. choices is an exact dict mapping every freeze result ID, and no other IDs, to a native integer in that operand's unsigned bit-pattern range. Supplied choices are explicit witnesses for otherwise arbitrary freeze outcomes, not a prediction of a real compiler's choice. Inputs satisfy these additional subset restrictions at each executed step for the supplied choices: add/eq operands and select conditions are concrete or poison, never undef. Undef can occur as a literal, a select arm/result, a freeze input, or the final branch condition. All operations execute in list order. An unflagged add of concrete operands wraps modulo 2**bits. With nsw=True, interpret both bit patterns as signed two's-complement integers and produce poison if their mathematical sum is outside [-2**(bits-1),2**(bits-1)-1]; otherwise return the wrapped bit pattern. A poison operand makes add return poison of the operand width, and makes eq return poison of width 1. Concrete eq returns width-1 value 1 or 0. Select with a concrete condition copies the yes value for 1 and no value for 0, without propagating poison from the unselected arm; a poison condition produces poison of the arm width. Freeze preserves a concrete input unchanged and ignores its supplied choice; for poison/undef it produces a concrete value using choices[id]. Store that one dynamic result so all its later uses agree; separate freeze results may use different choices. Producing poison or undef alone is not immediate UB in this subset. At final br, poison or undef sets ub=True and branch=None; a concrete condition sets ub=False and branch to the corresponding native bool. With no branch, ub=False and branch=None. There are no other immediate-UB operations in the subset. Return exactly {values:{ID:{bits:int,kind:'value'|'poison'|'undef',value:int_or_None}},branch:bool_or_None,ub:bool}, including every definition in values. A poison/undef record always has value=None. All containers/scalars are exact native dict/list/str/int/bool/None values. Empty program/choices are valid. Do not mutate any input, including during later calls. All returned mutable records and call results must be fresh, independent and must not alias inputs. No outside-domain validation is required. Use only the standard library, with no actual compiler invocation, raw memory, threads or network. This reports the declared value semantics before optimizer refinements, not the observable behavior of an arbitrary source program.

Implement ssa_availability(entry, blocks, definitions, uses, parameters=None), a pure SSA operand-availability analyzer. blocks is an exact native dict of 1–8 block IDs, each mapped to exactly {size:int,successors:[block_IDs]}. size is 0–8 and counts nonterminator instruction positions 0..size-1; each block's control terminator is conceptually after those positions. Successors are distinct existing IDs. entry exists, has no incoming edges, and every supplied block is entry-reachable. Cycles and nonentry self-edges are allowed. IDs are case-sensitive ASCII matching [A-Za-z0-9_]{1,12}; block and value namespaces are separate. definitions is an exact dict of 0–32 value IDs to exact {block:B,position:i} records with an existing block and valid position; no two definitions occupy the same block/position. parameters is None by default, meaning no parameters, or a native list of at most 16 distinct value IDs disjoint from definitions. uses is a native list of at most 64 exact queries: {kind:'ordinary',value:V,block:B,position:i} or {kind:'phi',value:V,block:M,predecessor:P}. Ordinary positions are valid; every V is a parameter or supplied definition; each phi P is an actual predecessor of M. Queries ask only whether that operand would be available, and may return false. Compute ordinary block dominators over the complete CFG. Parameters are available at every query. For an ordinary use in another block, the defining block must dominate the use block. In the same block, the definition position must be STRICTLY earlier than the use position; equality is invalid. For a phi incoming query, test availability at the END of predecessor P: the defining block must dominate P. Every definition in P is before its terminator and is available on P's outgoing edge, regardless of destination instruction positions. A definition in one diamond arm can thus be valid on that arm's phi edge without dominating the merge, and a loop-header/body definition can be available on an appropriate dominated backedge. Return exactly {dominators:{block:[sorted_block_IDs]},available:[bool_in_query_order]}. Include every block's dominator set, including itself. Dominator lists use ordinary case-sensitive Python lexical sorting; dict ordering is irrelevant. Output containers, strings and booleans must be exact native dict/list/str/bool values. Input positions/sizes are native ints excluding bool; other inputs use native dict/list/str, plus optional parameters=None. Preserve duplicate queries and their positions. Every call returns fresh independent mutable containers that do not alias input or earlier result containers. Never mutate inputs, including during later calls, or retain cross-call result state. No invalid-input validation is required. This does not check operation types, complete phi incoming lists, phi placement, exception/invoke edge-defined results, unreachable blocks, or every LLVM verifier rule. Use only the standard library, with no real LLVM invocation, program execution, threads or network.

Implement guarded_vector_add(memory, dst, src, count, width=4), a deterministic declared vector-dispatch model, not real LLVM/SIMD execution. memory is one shared backing list of 0–32 native ints in 0..2**32-1. dst and src are native ints from 0 through len(memory); count is a native int 0–16 with dst+count<=len(memory) and src+count<=len(memory); width is a native int 1–8. All int domains exclude bool. Storage and lifetimes are valid, index arithmetic is mathematical/nonwrapping, and indices count u32 elements rather than bytes. The scalar source loop visits i=0..count-1 in increasing order: read CURRENT memory[src+i], add 1 modulo 2**32, then write memory[dst+i]. Choose the vector arm exactly when count==0 or dst+count<=src or src+count<=dst. Otherwise choose scalar, even if another proof could legally vectorize some overlap. On the vector arm execute floor(count/width) full groups in increasing order; each group reads ALL its source values before any group write, then writes wrapped outputs to corresponding destinations. Execute the remaining count%width iterations sequentially as a scalar epilogue. On the scalar arm execute ALL count iterations sequentially, with no vector groups. Return exactly {path,memory,vector_groups,scalar_steps,tail_count}. path is 'vector' or 'scalar'; memory is the full final fresh backing list, retaining untouched cells. Each group is exactly {indices:[iteration indices],inputs:[loaded values],outputs:[wrapped values]}. Each scalar step is exactly {index:iteration index,input:loaded value,output:wrapped value}; scalar_steps records only the epilogue on the vector arm, or all steps on scalar fallback. tail_count is count%width on the vector arm and 0 on scalar fallback. Zero count selects vector, changes no cell, and returns empty traces and tail_count 0. Traces preserve execution order. All containers/scalars have the exact built-in dict/list/str/int types stated. Every returned mutable container must be independent of inputs, other returned mutable containers and earlier call results; inputs must remain unchanged during this and later calls. Inputs satisfy the complete domain; no outside-domain validation is required. Use only the standard library and ordinary Python computation/allocation, with no real compiler, vector hardware, raw memory, threads or network.

Implement deopt_trace(machine, metadata, program, committed), a symbolic straight-line integer source-VM reconstruction model inspired by the dated Maglev frame-state mechanism. It is not V8/JavaScript emulation, actual machine-code execution, or rollback. machine is exactly {registers,stack}: registers maps at most 8 IDs to native u32 words in 0..2**32-1, and stack is a list of at most 8 such words. metadata is exactly {pc,locals}: pc is a native int from 0 through len(program), identifying the NEXT UNEXECUTED instruction; locals maps at most 8 names to recipes. Leaf recipes are exactly {kind:'constant',value} with a native integer in [-2**31,2**32-1], {kind:'register',name,format:'i32'|'u32'}, or {kind:'stack',slot,format:'i32'|'u32'}. Referenced registers exist; slot is a native integer index with 0<=slot<len(machine['stack']). A u32 recipe returns the word unchanged. An i32 recipe returns word when word<2**31, otherwise word-2**32. The only composite recipe is {kind:'add',left:leaf,right:leaf}; it sums decoded leaves as exact mathematical integers. Nested adds are excluded. Recipes read the immutable checkpoint, never other reconstructed locals, so recipe dictionary order is irrelevant. program is a list of at most 16 instructions: exactly {op:'add',local,delta} with native integer delta in [-1000,1000], or {op:'emit',local,label}. Every local mentioned anywhere in program exists in metadata.locals. IDs and labels are case-sensitive ASCII strings matching [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,16}; register, local and label namespaces are independent, and repeated effect labels are allowed. All integer domains exclude bool. committed is a list of at most 16 exact {label,value} records with native integer values in [-2**40,2**40]. They are already-completed visible effects in original order, possibly including earlier caller history. The caller guarantees reconstructed locals and committed form a valid checkpoint after instructions before pc. If pc names an instruction, that next source instruction has not run; pc==len(program) is an already-completed continuation. No checkpoint-validity or other outside-domain validation is required. Reconstruct locals purely, preserve committed effects and emit an initial snapshot. Then execute program[pc:] exactly once in increasing order. add changes only its named local with exact mathematical integer arithmetic, without u32 wrapping. emit appends {label,value:current named local value}. Reconstruction itself must not replay any source instruction or emit. Return a native list containing the initial snapshot and one snapshot AFTER each suffix instruction. Each snapshot is exactly {pc,locals,effects}, with pc advanced after the executed instruction. At pc==len(program), return only the initial snapshot. There is no implicit restart or final cleanup. All containers/scalars have the stated exact built-in dict/list/str/int types. Every returned mutable container must be independent of inputs, other returned mutable containers and earlier results; inputs remain unchanged during this and later calls. Use only the standard library and ordinary Python computation/allocation, with no real compiler/runtime, raw memory, threads or network.

Implement dce_slice(entry, blocks, parameters=None), a conservative effect/control-preserving instruction slice. blocks is an exact native dict of 1–8 block IDs. Each block is exactly {instructions:[records],successors:[block_IDs],profile_count:int}, with a nonempty instruction list and 1–64 instructions total. Instructions are exactly {id:ID,kind:'pure'|'effect'|'branch'|'return',uses:[value_IDs]}; instruction IDs are globally unique. IDs are case-sensitive ASCII matching [A-Za-z0-9_]{1,12}; block and value namespaces are separate. Every block ends with exactly one branch or return; earlier instructions are pure/effect. A branch has one or two distinct existing successors, with respectively zero or one operand. A return has no successors and zero or one operand. Pure/effect instructions have at most eight operands, with duplicates allowed, and their IDs define values; branch/return IDs cannot be used as values. parameters is None by default, meaning empty, or a native list of at most 16 distinct value IDs disjoint from all instruction IDs. Every operand names a parameter or a pure/effect result. Reachable uses already have valid ordinary SSA availability: a same-block producer is strictly earlier, or its block dominates the use block. No phi, invoke, exceptional/indirect edges or hidden entries are modeled; no other type/verifier checks are required. entry exists and has no predecessors; other unreachable blocks and CFG cycles are allowed. profile_count is a native int 0–10000, never bool. Counts are supplied prior-execution annotations without a future-execution guarantee; no flow-consistency constraint is imposed. Pure instructions are total, nontrapping and effect-free. Every effect instruction has a required observable action if its block executes, even when its result is unused. Every reachable branch and return is a required control root. First compute structural reachability from entry through ALL supplied successors, completely ignoring profile_count. Remove every instruction in unreachable blocks, including their effects. In reachable blocks, root liveness at every effect, branch and return, then repeatedly retain every instruction producing an operand of a retained instruction. Parameters need no producer. Remove exactly the unmarked pure instructions in reachable blocks. Do not fold conditions, change the CFG, remove a reachable terminator, or interpret zero observations as impossibility. Return exactly {reachable:[sorted_block_IDs],kept:{reachable_block:[kept_instruction_IDs_in_original_order]},removed:[sorted_instruction_IDs]}. Include exactly reachable block keys in kept; removed includes all nonretained IDs, including unreachable control/effect instructions. Sorting uses ordinary case-sensitive Python lexical ordering; dict order is irrelevant. Returned containers and strings are exact native dict/list/str values. Inputs use exact native dict/list/str/int values plus optional parameters=None. Every call returns fresh independent mutable containers that do not alias inputs or earlier outputs. Never mutate inputs, including during later calls, or retain cross-call result state. No outside-domain validation is required. Use only the standard library, without actual compilation, program execution, memory effects, threads or network. This is the stated conservative slice, not maximal DCE, a branch-feasibility prover or a full LLVM optimization pipeline.
